run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:17:37Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by a real but small stream of HTTP 503s generated by the frontend-proxy ingress (Envoy). In the alert window only the server-side ingress spans of frontend-proxy carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR (~20.3 error spans over 13:17:37–14:27:28, all SPAN_KIND_SERVER; the client-side 'router frontend egress' spans show 0), and the pod's access log shows the matching failures: '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward upstream cluster 'frontend' (100.71.53.109:8080, i.e. the frontend Service whose only endpoint is pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 at 100.96.2.93:8080). The failures start at 13:53:30 (log) / 13:54:37 (span metrics) — about 36 minutes before the alert — persist intermittently (up to 7.8 error spans per 5m) and fall back to 0 at the last evaluated point, 14:26:37. The frontend workload itself is Running with restartCount 0 and its own spans record no errors and no durations above 2 s, so the frontend's only visible fault signal is that its HTTP connections are terminated before a response starts. The frontend container is capped at 100m CPU and is throttled in 22–31% of CFS periods throughout the window (the highest of the 22 otel-demo pods), which is a plausible contributing cause but not a proven one. Numerically the alert annotation (0.0111) could not be reproduced from the available series (service-wide 5m ERROR ratio at 14:17:37 was 0.00038), and no Prometheus alerting rules are loaded, so the alert's exact expression is unknown.

claims.text: In the 10 minutes ending 14:27:28, frontend-proxy spans with span_name 'ingress' (span_kind SERVER) totalled increase 3753.59 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 2.23 with STATUS_CODE_ERROR, while span_name 'router frontend egress' (span_kind CLIENT) totalled 3758.06 UNSET and 0 ERROR — the error signal exists only on the ingress server spans.

Over the whole window 13:17:37–14:27:28 the ERROR span increase for service_name frontend-proxy was 20.29 spans on span_name 'ingress' and 0 on 'router frontend egress'; grouped by span_kind it was 20.29 for SPAN_KIND_SERVER and 0 for SPAN_KIND_CLIENT.

The frontend-proxy ingress ERROR rate was 0 at every 5-minute point from 13:48:37 through 13:53:37, first became non-zero (1.111) at 13:54:37, peaked at 7.778 at 14:03:37, stayed intermittently non-zero (last value 1.211) until 14:25:37 and was 0 at the final point 14:26:37.

The frontend-proxy container log of pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth contains 10 responses of '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward upstream cluster 'frontend' (upstream host 100.71.53.109:8080) between 13:53:30.642 and 14:01:42.352, for paths GET /, /api/products/* and /api/data/?contextKeys=*, each with 0 request bytes, 95 response bytes and upstream durations of 240–705 ms; no 5xx line appears earlier in the read portion, which starts at 13:17:37.

The Service 'frontend' in otel-demo has ClusterIP 100.71.53.109 port 8080 and exactly one endpoint, address 100.96.2.93 targeting pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2, so the 503s logged by frontend-proxy are directed at that single frontend pod.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 is Running with restartCount 0 and startTime 13:36:39Z, owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5; the frontend Deployment reports replica 1 ready and available, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend.
The frontend container is configured with limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and requests cpu 50m / memory 100Mi; the frontend-proxy container has limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi.

Over 13:17:37–14:27:28 the frontend pod was CPU-throttled in 0.281 of its CFS periods, the highest ratio of the 22 otel-demo pods (next: postgresql 0.236, cart 0.233), while frontend-proxy was throttled 0.0496.

The frontend pod's throttling is steady rather than bursty: its 5-minute throttle ratio stays between 0.22 and 0.31 at every point from 13:52:28 to 14:26:28, with CPU usage around 0.048–0.052 cores against the 0.1-core limit.
Frontend span durations show no elevation: 0.99992 of frontend spans were ≤2000 ms at 13:52:00 (5m window) and 1.0 of them were ≤2000 ms at 14:17:37.

The frontend Deployment rolled a new ReplicaSet at 14:08:27–14:08:28 (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate of load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb and SuccessfulDelete of load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89), i.e. a controller-driven rollout of load-generator 14 minutes after the frontend-proxy 503s began.

The service-wide ERROR ratio computed from the only available request metric for frontend-proxy was 0.00038 at 14:17:37 over 5 minutes (ERROR rate divided by all-span rate), and the only metric names present for this target are 63 in total, none of them an http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count series.

Normal traffic through the same frontend-proxy pod returns 200 and 308 (for /api/data/?contextKeys=* redirects) with response code details via_upstream, so the 503 UC responses are a small minority of requests on the same upstream.

The frontend workload shows no failure in its own telemetry: its spans have zero ERROR increase over the window, none of its exported spans exceed 2000 ms at 14:17:37, and its pod has restartCount 0 and is Running, so the evidence of a frontend-side fault is limited to the Envoy ingress log's upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} detail rather than to any frontend error or latency reading.

Primary hypothesis: the frontend HTTP server in pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 closes or resets kept-alive connections before sending a response, so Envoy in frontend-proxy records 503 with flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; this matches the intermittent, low-volume pattern (10 logged 503s in 13:53:30–14:01:42, ~20 error spans over the window), the absence of any frontend restart, and the fact that both successful 200/308 and failing 503 responses share the same upstream.

Second hypothesis: the frontend container's 100m CPU limit leaves it CPU-throttled in roughly a quarter of CFS periods (0.281 over the window, 0.22–0.31 per 5m), which could delay request handling enough to lose the keepalive race; the weaknesses are that throttling is constant while the 503s are intermittent and that no frontend latency elevation is visible in the exported spans.

The load-generator rollout at 14:08:27 did not cause the frontend-proxy 503s: the first 503 appears in the frontend-proxy log at 13:53:30 and the first non-zero error-span point is 13:54:37, about 14 minutes before the Deployment scaled down load-generator-57ffcd644 and created load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb, and the error counts remain in the same 0–7.8 per 5m band across the rollout.

A frontend container crash, OOM kill or restart is not the cause: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 is Running with restartCount 0 since 13:36:39Z and the only events in the namespace during the window concern the load-generator rollout; no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or BackOff event for frontend was returned.

A stale or wrong Service endpoint is not the cause: the frontend Service endpoint list contains exactly one address, 100.96.2.93, which matches the running frontend pod IP, so Envoy is routing to the live pod rather than a dead endpoint.

gaps: No Prometheus alerting or recording rules are loaded for this target (list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered call), so the alert's expression and the annotated value 0.0111 could not be reproduced; the only reproducible service-level ratio at 14:17:37 from available series is 0.00038.

Jaeger holds no traces for this window after about 13:50:55 (searches for frontend-proxy in 14:10:00–14:20:00 and 13:47:37–14:27:28 returned no traces later than 13:50:53), so the failing requests' traces, their parent spans and any downstream chain could not be inspected.

The frontend container produced no log lines in the window (0 bytes read, filter not run), so an application-side record of connection resets, keepalive timeouts or handler errors could not be checked.

frontend-proxy's Envoy bootstrap/keepalive configuration is not stored in any otel-demo ConfigMap (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist), so upstream idle/keepalive timeout settings could not be verified.
The frontend-proxy access-log read hit the 4 MiB limit at 14:05:36, so 503 lines between 14:05:36 and 14:27:28 are unknown; only the span-metric series show errors continuing in that period.

No comparable baseline exists inside the authorized window before 13:17:37 (span-metric series returned no data for 12:17:37–13:17:37), so it is unknown whether this 503 rate is new or chronic for this deployment.
The alert's reported error ratio (0.0111) and the observed span-based error ratio differ by roughly a factor of 30; which denominator or window Alertmanager used is unknown.

Whose of the frontend's dependencies (cart 0.233 and postgresql 0.236 CFS throttling) contributed to the request handling behaviour could not be tested: no cart/postgresql ERROR series were returned and no slow frontend spans were observed.
next_steps: Inspect the frontend-proxy (Envoy) bootstrap configuration for upstream HTTP/1.1 keepalive and idle timeouts and compare them with the frontend Node.js server keepAliveTimeout, since a keepalive close race is the best-fitting mechanism for 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}.

Review whether the frontend Deployment's 100m CPU limit is appropriate for its load, given ~0.05 cores of steady usage and 22–31% CFS throttling; test raising the limit and observe whether the 503 UC rate drops.

Fetch the Alertmanager rule definition for RequestErrorRate to confirm which metric, window and denominator produce 0.0111, and align it with traces_span_metrics_calls_total so the alert and the observable error rate are comparable.
Capture frontend container logs or enable stdout logging for the frontend pod so the server side of terminated connections can be observed directly.
Fix the trace pipeline retention so Jaeger keeps traces up to the alert time; currently nothing after ~13:50:55 is available for this window.
